title: Night Caboose — runbook draft and quick log
body:
Purpose: quick, compact handoff notes for late-night bridge (meant to be glued to a monitor). Informal, intentionally terse — expand into proper runbook later.

Shift context:
- Host: hosted-api + a small dedicated pool for customer X. Traffic steady but spiky around 00:30 UTC.
- Known fragility: KV cache thrash on LLM-2k when multiple long-prefix requests flow; batching can help but increases tail latency for small requests.
- Current alert posture: all green except sporadic 503s on /v1/stream for model:llama-quad-16q.

Open items at start of shift:
- Scaling policy for dedicated-pool-dynamo is still using default cooldown 5m (ticket CON-1423). If we see sustained 90th p95 token latency > 400ms, manually bump min-replicas by +2.
- Nina investigating small regression in live evals for codegen flows (linked in Slack thread). Might want to pin codegen v2 -> v2-fallback if errors spike.

Quick triage flow (three-minute checklist):
1) Check global service overview dashboard (Console -> Routes -> last 60m). Look for sudden error-rate jump, model-specific 5xx.
2) If 5xx concentrated on a single model variant, switch route fallback to compatible variant: console -> routing -> select route -> fallback policy -> choose "compatible-variant" -> apply.
3) If errors are region-specific, check region health (us-west-2 / eu-central-1) and failover logs (trace id prefix: region-fail-).
4) If no obvious route issues, tail inference logs for the failing requests (use centralized logging): rg "model=llama|error|timeout" /var/log/ingestion/*.log or use Kibana query below.

Common Kibana queries (copy-paste):
- 5xx by model: status:>=500 AND response.model.keyword: *llama* AND timestamp:[now-1h TO now]
- streaming timeouts: route:/v1/stream AND json.error: "client_stream_timeout"

Fast fixes (order matters):
- If high 5xx and errors indicate OOM on pod: scale up GPU nodes for the pool (infra playbook). Command: scale dedicated-pool-dynamo minReplicas +2 via Console (or k8s: kubectl -n inference scale deploy/dynamo-pool --replicas=<current+2>).
- If streaming timeouts only, increase keep-alive on gateway: edit configmap gateway-timeouts -> stream_idle_timeout: 90s -> rollout gateway (kubectl rollout restart deploy/gateway).
- If sudden latency spike but errors low: temporarily reduce batching window to prioritize latency (Console -> optimize -> batching -> set targetWindowMs to 8ms for route). Monitor 1m SLA.
- If model variant flakey: flip to last-known-good using rollout -> canary rollback -> promote previous version. Note: promote triggers KV cache cold-start, expect short blip.

Escalation matrix (who to @):
- First contact: on-call SRE (Samir Kapoor) — paging 10m after persistent >10% error rate.
- If infra (node OOM, scheduler eviction): infra lead (Priya Reddy).
- If model quality regression or hallucinations on customer-critical route: applied-ml lead (Dr. Kenji Ito).

Short-term patches to keep traffic alive:
- Route split + degrade: create traffic-split rule to send 20% of requests to a cheaper small-quantized variant (llama-quad-8q) to relieve pressure. Dial down to 0% after stabilization.
- Cache safeguard: enable prefix-only KV caching for the route for 5m to reduce KV churn (Console -> cache -> prefix-only).

Diagnostic commands (most-used):
- kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --show-labels | rg dynamo
- kubectl -n inference logs deploy/dynamo-pool -c runtime --since=30m | tail -n 200
- kubectl -n gateway get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 50
- rli query "errors.count{route='/v1/generate',region='us-west-2'}@1h"

Notes-to-self / gotchas:
- Rolling restart of pool can cause cold KV cache and temporarily double token cost for hot routes. Warn product/CS if doing during business hours.
- Autoscaler sometimes overshoots when batch size changes; prefer manual bump for short incidents.
- When flipping variants, check for tokenization mismatch (customer integrations may assume old tokenization).

Post-incident checklist (to fill if an incident happened):
- Timestamp incident start/end
- Root cause hypothesis + logs snippet (copy URL to Kibana)
- Actions taken (scale, restart, variant flip) + who authorized
- Customer impact summary and customers notified (CS rep)
- Follow-up tasks (open tickets, postmortem owner)

Personal TODO (expand into proper doc):
- Draft a concise "latency vs batching" decision tree for on-call (1 page) — link to optimize page.
- Formalize dedicated-pool cooldown override play (CON-1423 followup).
- Add a one-click rollback button to Console for variant flips (prod-ux proposal).

Random fast notes: 
- If you see a repeated signature: "error: runtime::KVCacheMiss - prefix_keys>1000" consider reducing prefix indexing for that model.
- Keep an eye on nightly job that purges stale cache entries (~03:00 UTC). If purge fails, you will see cache growth and slow downs by 04:00.

End-of-shift handoff checklist (to next oncall):
- State any ongoing mitigations (e.g., "scaled dynamo +2 at 2026-03-12T01:05Z, monitoring p95").
- Point out open tickets and expected follow-ups.
- Call out any experiments running (canary percent, routing tweaks).

Sign-off: A. Martinez — leave a 1-line summary in #oncall-bridge thread, include any ask (pages to watch).

---
Loose scratch: last night we saw a pattern where small single-token requests were batched into 256-token windows causing high p95; investigate batching heuristics by client-identifier (some SDKs send many micro-requests).

End.
